abstract:
Henningson [1] and Anderson–Henningson [2] studied the Haydys–Witten (HW) and Kapustin–Witten (KW) equations on $\mathbb R_s	imes S^3	imes I$ with Nahm poles at both ends of the interval, for $SU(2)$ fields that are left-invariant on $S^3$ and equivariant under the diagonal $SO(3)$. They found exactly two gauge-inequivalent static solutions above a critical length, which merge at that length and are absent below it. They computed the period expansion, predicted a five-dimensional tunneling instanton joining the two solutions, and derived its leading profile formally; rigorous existence was left open [2].
We prove that this instanton exists. With radius $r$ and interval length $L$, and for $\pi r<L<\pi r+\delta$, there is an isotropic HW solution with the following properties. It is smooth, has Nahm poles at both ends uniformly in $s$, converges exponentially to the two KW solutions as $s	o\mp\infty$, and has energy $	frac{8\sqrt{10}}{5}\pi^2r^3L^{-2}
u^{3/2}(1+o(1))$, where $
u=(L/r)^2-\pi^2$. Up to translation it is the unique nonconstant solution near the degenerate static solution. Its linearization in the isotropic class is Fredholm of index $1$ and surjective. For self-containedness we also reprove the static classification from [1, 2].
The proof is a Kirchgässner–Mielke centre-manifold reduction in the form of Haragus–Iooss. The hypotheses we verify are: the linear operator is limit point at both ends, hence self-adjoint; it has compact resolvent; and its kernel is spanned by $\sin^2(\pi y/L)$. The parameter enters through a hyperbolic forcing, which we remove by the explicit shift $w_
u=	frac{i
u}{6\pi}\sin(2\pi y/L)$. In the new coordinates the centre manifold is fully tangent, and the reduced field is $\dot x=	frac56x^2-	frac43
u-	frac{
u^2}{54\pi^2}+\dots$. Transversality follows from a block reduction of the variational equation to a scalar operator, with an estimate on the size of the perturbation.
We do not treat non-isotropic deformations, half-lines or knots. An exact verifier runs 61 checks and reports FALLOS = 0.

change_summary: Corrections only; no new claims. (1) Citations to Anderson-Henningson [2] corrected against the published JHEP02(2012)063 version: the period expansion is Eq. (3.8) (not (3.34)); the leading tunneling profile is Eqs. (4.7), (4.10), (4.11) and the second-order dynamical correction Eqs. (4.12)-(4.13) (not (4.51)-(4.52), which do not exist); the dictionary cos^2(y/2) = sin^2(pi tau) under y = 2 pi tau - pi is stated (lines in Sec. 1 and Sec. 6). (2) Proposition 5.3 now invokes the Hilbert-space centre-manifold theorem [9, Ch. 2, Thm. 2.20] (Hypotheses 2.1, 2.4 and estimate (2.9); (2.10) not needed, Remark 2.16) with X = Y = L^2, instead of Hypothesis 2.7, as the referee requested; the parameter version Thm. 3.3 is applied to the extended system. (3) Sec. 7 Step 3: 2 int zeta^3 Re w corrected to 2 int zeta^2 Re w (the coefficient 5/3 x is unchanged). (4) Consistency check after Lemma 5.4: the normalization of H is specified (x = -pi r^3 H + O((r^3 H)^3)). (5) Sec. 2: the self-dual 2-form is B = ds ^ phi + *_3 phi on the transverse slice R_s x X. (6) Sec. 10 (Limitations): the isotropic scope of Theorem D is emphasized with a citation to the later rStation paper math_30 [18], which shows a four-dimensional cokernel in the complete gauge-fixed space; reference [18] added.
title: Rigorous existence, local uniqueness and transversality of the Anderson–Henningson tunneling instanton on $\mathbb R\times S^3\times I$
